title: Meeting Bunk in Lake Charles at Tony Babin's band
summary: During the high water she lived in Lake Charles, met Bunk at a dance when he joined the band from Electra, Texas; he had her launder his shirts and began visiting. They returned to New Iberia in 1932.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah, because through him, that's the way I met Bunk. Oh, is that right?
Yeah. That's what I'd like to know, if you can tell about that while we're talking.

Well, I was- we were in Lake Charles at that time. I think that was in 1929. It was during the high water, we went to Lake Charles for the high water. It was in 27, I think. Oh, yes, there was a big flood in 27, I remember that. Yeah, in Iberia. Well, we was in Lake Charles, and we stayed over there. And then my mother came up there during the high water. See, I was up there a little before, living with my sister. Is your sister older than you? Yeah, she's older than me. And I quite, I used to go to dances and things. And when Bunk first came to Tony's Bob-Amband in Lake Charles, Louisiana, well, that's where I met him that night. Where was he playing? In Tony's Bob-Amband, in the Lake Charles band. I forgot the other name of it, but I knew it was Tony's Bob-Amband.
Yes. Was one of the called the Eagles, and then there was Ebon Thomas. No, that's not the one.
That's not the one. No, this was a little band in Lake Charles. He had came from, he had just came from Electric, Texas. Electric, Texas.
Yeah. That's where I heard he had been there. I was not even talking to him.

Because he was over there, he said he was working at an undertaker place there. And they wrote for him to come and join this band, and that's where he came there. And so the next day, my brother-in-law brought him over to the house. He asked my brother-in-law who I was. And I told my brother-in-law had knew him, you know, a long time before. So he came on to the house, and he started talking. And then he asked me, would I mind doing him up some shirts? So I told him, yeah. And so he brought the shirts over to my house, and I did up the shirts fine. And then he was living, he had a room, a three-room house right on Pine Street then, because he always did, before living to himself, he said, and not in a rooming house. And he had furniture and everything there. So when I, when I, he came and got the shirts, he thought they were so nicely done. And then from that on he came, kept on coming to see me.
How long did he stay there? Played there quite a while.
Yeah, he played there about a year or two. And then after that.
Did you stay over there and live over there too? Yeah. After the high water too?
Yeah, we lived over there. We came home in 1932. Came back to New Iberia.
